label: Medieval
title: The Secret of Torre Umbría
premise: Torre Umbría, a stone castle in the sierras of Castile, has been cut off for weeks by the snows of a cruel winter. Beneath its roof live the lord of the place, his household and the grudges the cold has piled up. Tonight the chapel bell is tolling for the dead.

art.style: painterly 14th-century Castilian illustration, flickering torchlight and candlelight against cold winter-blue shadows, rough stone and timber textures, ochre, oxblood and slate-grey palette, realistic proportions

victim.name: Gonzalo de Umbría
victim.description: Lord of Torre Umbría and of the villages in the valley, a widower and a veteran of the border campaigns. Hard on his vassals, suspicious of his own household and miserly with everything but his honour, he ruled the castle with an iron hand and went over in person the accounts others preferred not to look at.

people.name: Leonor del Valle
people.personality: Cold, exact and proud of her office: the keys, the larder and the household’s petty accounts all depend on her. Speaks formally and correctly, in short, complete sentences, never raising her voice. Corrects others with a single word, invokes the custom of the house as if it were law and concedes nothing that is not proven to her. Never invents: when she doesn’t know something, she says so.
people.appearance: A middle-aged woman, tall and very upright, with a gaunt face, thin lips and grey eyes that never blink. Her greying chestnut hair is gathered under a starched white linen wimple. She wears a dark grey wool gown, belted with leather, from which hangs a heavy bunch of iron keys.

rooms.name: Great hall
rooms.description: A fireplace big enough to roast an ox half-warms the hall, and the smoke clings to the hunting tapestries and blackened beams. It smells of oak logs, tallow candles and the dry rushes strewn across the floor.
ambience: As you enter, the heat of the fire hits your face while your back stays frozen. An oak log splits and spits sparks across the flagstones.
The rushes crackle under your boots. In a corner, a hunting dog lifts its head, looks at you a moment and curls up again by the embers.

Your footsteps echo down the nave as if someone were walking behind you. Wax drips from a taper, and outside the wind makes the narrow window moan.

motives: Had forged a deed of gift to get hold of the mill and the river lands. {victim} had uncovered the fraud and meant to bring it before the king’s bailiff the next day.
Had sold a neighbouring lord the strength and watch rota of the castle guard. {victim} had intercepted the letter and meant to denounce the treason before the king’s justice the next day.
Had for years been skimming part of the grain rents and tithes of the lordship. {victim} had ordered the accounts checked and meant to demand repayment before the council the next day.
Had secretly used the lord’s seal to borrow a large sum from a Burgos merchant. {victim} had received the claim and meant to denounce the forgery before the bailiff the next day.

Had opened the postern by night to the bandits who plundered the granary in the autumn. {victim} had recognised one of them among the prisoners and meant to get the accomplice’s name out of him the next day.

arrivals: You reach Torre Umbría with the last of the light, your mule sunk to its hocks in snow. The portcullis rises with a screech of chains and the courtyard greets you with the smell of smoke and frozen dung. You carry a letter under the king’s seal: you are his investigator.

You cross the drawbridge wrapped in your travelling cloak, the sierra wind cutting at your face. Above the gate, the arms of the Umbrías can barely be made out beneath the frost. A groom takes your reins without meeting your eye.

The blizzard forces you to seek shelter at the nearest castle, and that castle is Torre Umbría. The torches on the wall-walk shiver in the falling snow. By the fire they serve you hot spiced wine while your boots dry.

You have come from Burgos on an errand for the chancery and meant to spend just one night here. The chapel bells are ringing for Vespers as you cross the castle yard, and on the battlements the snow is beginning to cover everything.
tensions: Outside, the snow has closed the mountain pass: nobody leaves Torre Umbría until you say so. Weary faces watch you from the gloom, and one of them knows more than it lets on.
The porter bars the great gate with a dull thud. Within these walls, every glance is a suspicion and every silence half a confession.
You ask for paper, ink and a candle. Before dawn you must sort the lies from the truths, and in this castle both wear the same clothes.

night: The snow is falling thick and silent now. In the castle yard, a groom drags a bundle of firewood and leaves a furrow that fills in at once.
The candles in the great hall have burnt halfway down. Nobody goes to bed: the household talks in low voices by the fire and falls silent as you pass.
The wind rises off the sierra. It whistles between the merlons, rattles the shutters and sets the torches on the wall-walk trembling.
A dog howls in the stables and another answers. The porter walks the wall with a lantern, its light lost now and then in the blizzard.
The blizzard batters the tower in fury. The flames cower in their sconces, the fire in the hearth half dies and the cold creeps along the passages.
Suddenly the wind falls silent. In the hush there is only the sputter of the chapel lamp, and the whole castle seems to hold its breath.
epilogues: You speak the name of {culprit} in the great hall, and the silence falls like a slab of stone. The porter steps forward, the bar still in his hand, and awaits your signal. {culprit} offers no resistance, only lifts their gaze to the fire, as if seeking in the embers an excuse that no longer exists. Two men-at-arms close ranks around them, and their footsteps fade down the stairs towards the dungeon. When at last you sit down to write, the wind has dropped and a grey light is breaking over the sierra.

You gather the household in {scene} and set out, point by point, what the night has taught you. When you finish, {culprit}’s hands are shaking, and no one in the room dares meet their eye. The porter approaches slowly, without shoving, and with a gesture points to the stairs. The chapel bell tolls for {victim}, now with every reason. Outside it has stopped snowing, and the valley wakes white and calm.

At dawn the porter lifts the bar from the great gate for the first time in weeks: a timid sun is beginning to open the mountain pass. They lead {culprit} into the yard, hands bound, eyes fixed on the snow. You will set it all down in your report to the king, under your seal and signature. As the others return to their tasks, the household cross themselves when passing {scene}. At last, after so long a night, someone lights the kitchen fire.
